problem: Real-world fast-moving RGB-only navigation policies trained with RL depend on pre-trained visual encoders, but it is unclear which encoders and which feature projections matter, how much visual information is actually needed, and whether they transfer to a real robot.
motivation: Robotics builds on computer-vision pre-training, yet RL from actions alone gives a weak learning signal and pre-trained features are high-dimensional and opaque. The authors ran a large real-robot study (a real building, 0.7 m/s, RGB only) with realistic motion modelling in simulation to test which encoder and projection choices survive sim2real.
key_idea: Freeze pre-trained ViTs and compress their patch features into a bottleneck of as little as one attention scalar per patch (Pure Attention Projection), which keeps navigation performance while giving interpretable affordance-like maps.
insight: Heterogeneously distilled encoders (Dune, AM-Radio) and VC-1 transfer best to the real robot, while DinoV2 and DinoV3 lag when trained from scratch. Bottlenecking helps sim2real: more read-out tokens raise sim scores but not real ones (Table ablationnumro), and PCA fails while spatial projectors (PAP, LPR) work. DinoV3 fails completely with CAP and with self-attention pooling but works with PAP/LPR, suggesting expressive projectors are hard to train from weak RL signal. Fine-tuning from a Lidar-privileged agent narrows the gaps between encoders.
method: Agent: frozen ViT features go to a projector, then a 2-layer GRU (memory 1024) that also takes the static point goal, odometry and previous action; a linear policy head over 28 discrete velocity pairs at 3 Hz, plus an auxiliary goal-prediction head. Trained with PPO in Habitat/HM3D.

Realistic dynamics: Habitat teleport motion is replaced by a second-order motion model identified from real robot trajectories, so simulated inertia matches the physical robot; this is what closes the sim2real gap.
Cross-attention pooling (CAP): K learned queries attend into the patch tokens with 4-head MHA (Perceiver-Resampler style), giving K·E values.

Pure Attention Projection (PAP): CAP without value projections, so the K softmax attention maps over patches (K·P scalars) are the only visual input. The maps are interpretable and act like affordance maps.
Other projectors: PCA (fixed top-C components per patch), Linear Patchwise Reduction (LPR: linear map of each patch to D scalars), and Self-Attention Pooling (SAP, an ablation).
Privileged pre-training: an agent is first trained for 800-850M steps on a 360° Lidar-like scan, then fine-tuned for 100M steps on RGB with the ViT frozen.
Evaluation: HM3D val in simulation (2,500 episodes) and a real office building (14 episodes × 3 runs per configuration) with SR, SPL and SCT.

setting.backbone: Frozen pre-trained ViT-B encoders (DinoV2, DinoV3, VC-1, DUNE, AM-RADIO v2.5) + trained projector + 2-layer GRU policy (RL); ResNet-18 half-width from scratch baseline
setting.model_size: ViT-B ~86-98M params (frozen) plus small trainable projector/GRU
setting.training_data: RL (PPO) in Habitat on 800 HM3D train scenes; 500M steps from scratch, or 800M-step Lidar-privileged pre-training + 100M-step RGB fine-tuning; no real data
setting.observation: Monocular forward RGB (160x120) + odometry (wheel encoders/IMU) + static point goal; no depth or Lidar
setting.action_space: 28 discrete velocity pairs (linear {0,0.2,0.4,0.7} m/s x angular -3..3 rad/s) at 3 Hz
setting.simulator: Habitat with HM3D and an identified second-order dynamics model; plus a real robot ('Rookie') in an office building
setting.privileged: none at test time (Lidar-like scan only used for pre-training in simulation; a safety mechanism using on-board 2D Lidar is used on the real robot but not fed to the agent)

numbers_note: Custom benchmark (static PointGoal in HM3D sim and a real building), not a canonical benchmark. Only a selection of configurations is listed; Table 4 in the paper contains placeholder 00.0 rows for CAP, which are not reported here.
results: Pre-trained frozen encoders with CAP reach about 85-91% SR in sim and 95-100% real SR (Dune, AM-Radio, VC-1), versus 53.5% SR for a ResNet trained from scratch, and sim and real numbers are comparable. Passing one attention scalar per patch (PAP) keeps sim SR near 86-89% and real SR at 92.9-100% for DinoV2. DinoV3 fails with CAP (0.0 SR) but reaches 79.7% SR with PAP K=8.
limitations: Only static point-goal navigation in a single real office building, with few real episodes per configuration (14×3) and a 1 m success radius in real runs versus 0.2 m in sim
The DinoV3 failure explanation is conjecture; the real-world evaluation excluded models below 60% sim SR, and the paper is a draft with placeholder table entries
The real robot uses an on-board Lidar safety mechanism (simulated during training) and an agent reset near the goal, which is not pure RGB-only end-to-end
